title: GO Command Center CONTROL_STATUS_V1
description: The compact, stable, read-only query contract a ChatGPT connector reads instead of the underlying JSON. Scope: CONTROL_STATE_AND_STATUS_ONLY. The required answer set is exactly the ten status questions plus request_channel; answers.request_fate is a supporting field that says why a submitted Request did not become a Task. Bounded in size, no execution parameter, and it can neither create nor sign a Task. It does NOT evaluate deploy or rollback readiness.

answers.description: Required = the ten question keys plus request_channel. All other keys are supporting fields and are never required.

hk_agent_recent_activity.description: Q1: the newest signed CONTROL_PLANE_HEALTH Evidence at any age. Activity, never liveness.

active_tasks.description: Q2: tasks published and still inside their validity window.

last_task.description: Q3: the newest signed Task of any class.

pr_tested.description: Q4/Q5: look up by_pr_number for a specific pull request.

repository_declared_runtime.description: Q7: what the repository declares. A declaration is never the truth about what is running.

runtime_verification.description: Q8: MATCH / DRIFT / NOT_RECENTLY_VERIFIED / UNKNOWN plus the image relation.

stuck_tasks.description: Q9: answer reads active_stuck_tasks only. Expired history never affects current health.

last_failure.description: Q10: kind is FAILED_RECORD or EXPIRED_WITHOUT_EVIDENCE.

request_channel.description: Which actions may currently be created, split by who creates them. A capability classification only; see out_of_scope.

human_request_actions.description: Actions a human / ChatGPT channel may express, each still subject to its own switch and gates.

platform_request_actions.description: Actions the platform's own bounded producer creates. Never a human execution right.

deploy_request_enabled.description: The DEPLOY Request is enabled and there is no switch to open: the authenticated Request is itself the authorisation. This is the contract-level answer, not the live-host state -- whether the host currently accepts one is a live-host fact, and a host with deployments suspended refuses the Request with deployment_authorization_mode_unsupported.

request_fate.description: CC V1-05. Why a Request did not become a Task, from the Bridge's own exported facts. Closed states; BECAME_A_TASK only with a signed Task behind it.

unbound_submissions.description: submissions the Bridge spoke about whose Request identity could not be established; no fact exists for them because a fact binds a request_id

hk_agent_online.description: Strict liveness. PROVEN only from a fresh signed probe; never inferred from a successful task.

x-go-notes: answers.hk_agent_online is derived only from fresh signed CONTROL_PLANE_HEALTH Evidence. answers.hk_agent_recent_activity reports the last signed activity at any age and is explicitly NOT liveness.
answers.repository_declared_runtime and answers.live_verified_runtime are separate objects. A repository pointer can never make the live runtime PROVEN.
answers.stuck_tasks.answer reads active_stuck_tasks only; recently and historically expired tasks are reported separately and never change the current-health answer.

answers.request_channel distinguishes known_capability from currently_enabled_request_action. HK_STAGING_DEPLOY is both proven and enabled: there is no deploy switch, so the connector may create a DEPLOY Request exactly as it may create a VERIFY, TEST_PR, CANARY or ROLLBACK one. It must not conclude from this that the host will accept it -- that is live_request_switch, a live-host fact, and the host answers with its own refusal token.

answers.request_fate reports why a Request did not become a Task, from facts the Bridge exported read-only. A Request file existing is not an acceptance: BECAME_A_TASK appears only when a signed Task on the control bus carries that Request's digest and verifies. A refusal carries the Bridge's own reason code, unmodified, and a duplicate or replay carries counted_as_success=false.
answers.repository_main_sha is UNKNOWN unless it was supplied out of band; the runtime's build-source SHA is never substituted for it.
Deploy readiness and rollback readiness are NOT computed here. No can_deploy, deployment eligibility, rollback target selection or release-gate verdict exists in answers.
This contract contains no image override, service name, compose path, shell command or signing parameter.
